title: Mesiri: from the drawing to the site
subtitle: Sales training: what Mesiri does with a building's drawings, and why a contractor pays for it
note: Internal use: shows a real customer's structural set (Kondotty). Narration is written in plain English and voiced in Malayalam (Sarvam mayura + bulbul:v3); technical words stay in English, as sites say them.

lines: In this video you will learn what Mesiri does with a building's drawings, in simple words, and why a contractor will pay for it.
No civil engineering background is needed. We go step by step.
Every building starts as drawings.
The architect draws the rooms: where the kitchen, the bedrooms and the toilets go.
Then a structural engineer draws the skeleton that holds the building up, and the steel inside it.
The contractor builds from these drawings, and the site engineer and workers follow them every day.
Four words are enough.
A footing is the wide concrete block buried under each pillar. It spreads the building's weight on the ground.
A column is the pillar standing on the footing.
Beams join the columns, and the slab is the floor and the roof.
All of it is concrete with steel bars inside. Concrete is bought in cubic metres, steel in kilos and cement in bags.
Today, three things go wrong on most sites.
One. The site builds from an old drawing, because the new revision was lost in a WhatsApp group. Breaking it and building again costs lakhs.
Two. A mistake in the drawing is found only after the concrete is poured.
Three. The owner does not know how far the work has reached, without going to the site.

scenes.value: Site never builds from an old drawing
lines: Mesiri fixes all three. First, the office drops the drawing PDF into Documents.
Mesiri reads the drawing number and the revision by itself, and files it under drawings.
When a new revision comes, the old one is marked out of date, and the history is kept.
Contracts and money papers are seen only by the office.
And anyone on site can ask on WhatsApp: send me the latest drawing. The right one comes back in seconds.

scenes.value: Mistakes caught before the concrete is poured
lines: Second, Mesiri checks the drawings before they reach the site. This is a real fifteen page structural set.
It reads every sheet, and compares the sheets with each other.
Here it found a real mistake. The detail of one footing calls both its columns C5, but the plan shows C5 and C6, and they have different steel.
Asking the engineer now costs one phone call. Finding it after the pour costs a demolition.

scenes.value: Order the right materials, without a quantity surveyor
lines: Third, Mesiri adds up the materials from the drawing.
For this building: twenty three footings, forty two cubic metres of concrete, one point eight tonnes of steel, and about three hundred and eighty bags of cement.
It shows every footing, with its size and the bars inside it. This usually takes a quantity surveyor days. Mesiri does it in seconds.
These numbers go into the BOQ and the material plan, so the contractor knows what to order, and by when.

scenes.value: No extra work for site: one WhatsApp message
lines: Fourth, and this is what customers love most. The drawing comes alive.
Every footing on the plan gets its grid name, like B3 or D5.
The site engineer sends one WhatsApp message, the same way they report work today: B3 footing concreted.
Mesiri understands it, even in Malayalam or Manglish, and saves it to footing B3 after one tap.

scenes.value: The owner sees progress on the drawing, from anywhere
lines: On the dashboard, footing B3 now turns green, on the engineer's own drawing. Yellow means work has started.
At the top: footings done, concrete placed and steel tied, out of the total.
Tap any footing to see who did what, and when, with the photos.
The owner sees the progress from anywhere, without going to the site.

scenes.value: Anyone can ask what is left, floor by floor
lines: The same works for floors and rooms.
First floor room two plastering done lands on that room, and the grid colours itself.
So the owner can simply ask on WhatsApp: what is left on the first floor? Mesiri answers room by room.
So, what does each person get?
The owner sees progress on the drawing, and stops losing money to rework.
The project manager always has the right drawing on site, and knows what to order.
The site engineer does nothing extra: one WhatsApp message, as today.
And the office keeps drawings, permits and contracts in one place.
How to demo it. Ask the customer for one structural drawing PDF, and drop it into Drawing check in front of them.
Show the mistakes it finds, and the steel and concrete it adds up.
Then send B3 footing concreted from your phone, and let them watch it turn green.
One thing to remember: Mesiri reads and adds up what is drawn. It never replaces the structural engineer's design.
Mesiri. From the drawing to the site, in one WhatsApp message.
